title: Minimalist Streaming Protocol & Tool Adapter — PRD Draft
summary: A compact PRD draft proposing a minimal streaming handshake and a thin tool-adapter surface for low-footprint client SDKs. Focus: predictable latency budget, graceful degradation, typed tool handoff, and pragmatic rollout plan for existing hosted API streaming features.
content:
Context
This is a working PRD for an alternate, intentionally minimalist streaming protocol and SDK adapter for tool-calling/structured-output use cases. Motivation: many embedded clients (mobile, edge) and third-party SDKs need a small, predictable client runtime and simple failure semantics; existing streaming designs are feature-rich but heavy. Aim: a narrow surface that covers 80% of low-latency tool-call scenarios with clear fallbacks and observability hooks.

Design goals (high level)
- Minimal wire-state: keep client state machine to 3 states (connecting, active stream, finalized/cleaned).
- Small framing: use compact delta frames for partial structured output instead of verbose JSON-chunk boundaries.
- Explicit tool lease tokens: lightweight token representing tool invocation lifecycle and idempotency (helps retries and offline replay).
- Latency-first: allow clients to specify a strict token-latency budget that the service uses to choose batching/caching tradeoffs and fallback policies.
- Clear degradation: single known fallback path — either (A) serialized non-streaming final response or (B) truncated partial response with tool resolution stub.
- Easy to implement on constrained runtimes (<=50kb client code).

Wire model overview
- Transport: WebSocket/HTTP-2 streams preferred; fall back to long-polling.
- Frame types (compact string identifiers):
  - open: {session_id, api_key_hint, model, lat_budget_ms, client_capabilities}
  - chunk: {seq, delta_type, payload_base64_or_json, lease_token?}
  - tool_call: {lease_token, tool_id, args_ref_or_inline}
  - tool_result: {lease_token, status, result_delta}
  - commit: {session_id, final_manifest}
  - heartbeat: {session_id, last_seq}
- Delta types: text, json-path-patch, kv-upsert, schema-marker. Delta frames allow small updates and schema hints without sending full object each time.

Tool adapter surface (SDK-facing)
- Goal: provide a very small JS/Swift/Kotlin wrapper that exposes 3 primitives:
  1) startStream(opts) -> StreamHandle
  2) onFrame(streamHandle, callback(frame))
  3) invokeTool(streamHandle, toolSpec) -> LeaseToken
- ToolSpec is intentionally minimal: {tool_id, arg_schema_ref, serialized_args (or remote_ref)}. The SDK serializes args and emits a tool_call frame. SDK returns LeaseToken (opaque string) so the application can show progress, cancel, or retry.
- SDK ergonomics: provide a single convenience function generateWithTools(prompt, tools, opts) which wires up stream lifecycle and maps tool_results back into a final JSON manifest. But this function is optional for minimal clients.

Structured output semantics
- The server maintains a working manifest (final object produced incrementally). Manifest is typed with a light schema (schema ids rather than full schemas in-wire) to keep updates small.
- Clients receive schema-marker deltas to understand expected shape before full fields arrive. This helps mobile renderers to show placeholders.
- Idempotency: lease_token serves as the transaction ID for a particular tool invocation. Replays with same lease_token must be treated as idempotent by tool runtimes.

Latency and fallback policy
- Clients can set lat_budget_ms at open. The routing layer uses this to decide:
  - aggressive prefix/KV cache lookup if lat_budget_ms < 150ms
  - allow batching windows up to 10ms if lat_budget_ms >= 150ms for throughput gains
- If the runtime cannot meet the lat_budget_ms with tools completed, server returns a deterministic fallback frame type: tool_stub which includes a short textual summary and a tool_status = partial. This is surfaced to SDK as an explicit partial-failure event.

Observability & telemetry (server + SDK)
- Minimal telemetry points the SDK emits: stream_open, first_byte_ms, tool_call_sent, tool_result_received, stream_commit, stream_error. Each includes session_id and lease_token (when applicable).
- Server emits: queue_delay_ms, backend_invoke_ms, kv_cache_hit boolean, model_variant. These are correlated via session_id.
- Telemetry payloads are small (base64 gzipped optional) to reduce bandwidth.

Security & privacy notes
- Lease tokens are short-lived (TTL tied to session) and bound to a session_id + client key. They are not sufficient to call privileged tooling without the session signature header.
- Tool arguments can be sent by remote_ref (pointer) to avoid shipping PII in the stream; remote_ref is a short server-side pointer that requires the same session to dereference.

Compatibility & migration path
- Backwards compatibility: server accepts existing streaming clients; this minimal protocol is exposed under a new version header (X-RI-Stream-Mode: minimalist-v1).
- Migrate flow: enable minimalist mode selectively per client via feature flag. Run A/B on low-latency cohorts (mobile and embedded).
- If a client is unable to support delta frames, we downgrade to chunk frames that contain full JSON snapshots at lower frequency.

Developer UX examples (JS pseudo)
- start = startStream({model: 'redwood-mini', lat_budget_ms: 120})
- start.on('frame', f => { if (f.type === 'tool_call') showToolProgress(f.lease_token); })
- tok = start.invokeTool({tool_id: 'search-v1', args: {q: 'population of NYC'}})
- // later receive tool_result frame referencing tok, and manifest gets patched via json-path-patch delta

Open questions (research + decisions)
- How large should lease_token be? Opaque 128-bit UUID vs human-friendly short tokens. Tradeoffs: size vs debuggability.
- Should the server provide automatic retry semantics for tool calls or leave retries entirely to client? Proposed: server may retry idempotent tools once when backend transient error; client informed via tool_result(status=retried).
- Delta encoding format: we propose json-path-patch but need to evaluate compact binary diff for mobile bandwidth savings.
- Versioning strategy for schema ids and delta types — lightweight registry vs embedding schema snippets in first frames.

Testing & rollout plan
- Phase 0 (lab): implement server-side minimalist wire mode behind feature flag; add SDK shim in playground JS and Android client. Run internal load tests with 20k concurrent mobile sessions.
- Phase 1 (canary): route 1% of production mobile traffic to minimalist-v1; measure first_byte_ms, tool_call success rate, and partial-failure rate.
- Phase 2: widen to 10% and test SDK usability with partner customers.
- Phase 3: full opt-in and provide migration doc + sample code.

Action items (next 4 sprints)
- Platform: implement delta frames and lease_token plumbing (infra + runtime) — Miguel (Sprint 1).
- SDK: build reference JS and Kotlin minimalist adapters (Aisha + Rowan, Sprint 1–2).
- Product: finalize fallback UX and billing implications for partial results (Sprint 2).
- SRE: add telemetry ingestion hooks and dashboards for session-level correlation (Sprint 2).

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally opinionated: smaller protocol with fewer bells and whistles. Expect tradeoffs in features (no built-in resume semantics in v1).
- We want feedback on the token model, delta format, and whether the lat_budget concept should be per-token or per-request.
